Article Title: 'Apologise to nation': Rijiju targets Congress after Army debunks Chinese intrusion claims
Article Text:
Army debunks fake AI video on China, Rijiju demands Congress apology

NEW DELHI: Bhartiya Janata Party on Tuesday hit out at the Congress for circulating an AI-generated video falsely attributing claims about Chinese control of areas in Arunachal Pradesh to an Indian Army officer, escalating the political face-off over the clip.Leading the BJP's counterattack, Union minister Kiren Rijiju accused the Congress of sharing the fabricated video featuring Lieutenant General Girish Kalia and demanded an apology for allegedly tarnishing the Army's image.In a post on X, Rijiju demanded an apology from the opposition party, writing, "Congress Party must apologize to the nation for spreading fake AI video to tarnish the image of Indian Army.""This is a treacherous act and is on par with the vile deeds of our enemies. The Congress Party is running a despicable campaign on behalf of India's enemies," the Union minister added.The row erupted after Congress shared a post on Monday alleging that China had captured the three areas in Arunachal Pradesh.Congress leader Ritu Choudhary on X wrote: "Shameful! Lieutenant General Girish Kalia (GOC, Spear Corps) says that China has captured Asafila, Longju, and Taksing circles in Arunachal Pradesh.Despite demands for logistics (supplies), there are reports that the army is being deployed against 'Gen Z' instead of China," Choudhary wrote.The Indian Army's fact-check unit also debunked the viral video, saying it had been digitally altered and contained fabricated remarks attributed to the officer.In a post on X, the Army said: "A digitally altered video is being circulated with fabricated remarks attributed to Lt Gen Girish Kalia, claiming that China has taken control of Asaphila, Longjou and Taksing Circle in Arunachal Pradesh and that the Indian Army has been denied essential supplies. The misleading video attempts to portray fabricated statements as a leaked admission by a senior Indian Army officer. The video uses Synthetic Generated Information to falsely attribute remarks to Lt Gen Girish Kalia. The original footage relates to a press briefing delivered by then GOC 28 Infantry Division, Maj Gen Girish Kalia, in Kupwara, Jammu & Kashmir, on 27 October 2023. He addressed infiltration attempts across the Line of Control, reporting 10 foiled attempts, the elimination of 27 terrorists and the recovery of warlike stores and narcotics.He made no such statements about Chinese control over Arunachal Pradesh or denial of supplies to the Indian Army..."The Army clarified that the original footage was from a press briefing held in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, on October 27, 2023, when then Major General Girish Kalia spoke about infiltration attempts across the Line of Control. According to the Army, he reported 10 foiled infiltration attempts, the elimination of 27 terrorists and the recovery of weapons and narcotics.The Army said the officer had made no statements about Chinese control over areas in Arunachal Pradesh or the denial of supplies to Indian troops.
Article Summary: Bhartiya Janata Party hits out at Congress for circulating fake AI video on China. Union minister Kiren Rijiju demands an apology for tarnishing the Army's image. Indian Army's fact-check unit also debunked the viral video, saying it had been digitally altered.

Article Title: 'Breaking Bad' to 'Prison Break': Stalin takes fresh swipe at Vijay govt after 17 inmates flee jail
Article Text:
Stalin doubles down on TV series jibes at Vijay govt after Theni jailbreak

How 17 inmates allegedly escaped

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin on Tuesday launched a fresh cinematic salvo at the ruling TVK government, following up his 'Breaking Bad' jibe with a 'Prison Break' reference to target chief minister C Joseph Vijay over the escape of 17 inmates from a Theni sub-jail.The DMK supremo's remarks came after 17 undertrial inmates allegedly escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Tamil Nadu's Theni district late on Monday night.Former CM hit out at the TVK government, accusing the administration of failing to maintain law and order.Taking a swipe at the government led by actor-turned-politician Vijay, Stalin drew a parallel with the television series Prison Break, saying the state appeared to be witnessing a similar situation after two prisoners had earlier escaped from Puzhal prison.“Following Breaking Bad, Prison Break has now begun in Tamil Nadu too!” Stalin said in a post on X, questioning how such a large number of inmates could escape despite improved security arrangements and surveillance systems.He said the escape of 17 inmates was particularly alarming, mentioning that it was reportedly the first such incident since 1995. Stalin said the incident came soon after the escape of two prisoners from Puzhal prison, raising questions over prison security.Accusing the government of incompetence, the former chief minister said authorities had failed to keep track of criminals released on bail and were now struggling to prevent escapes from inside jails.“Criminals outside are committing crimes freely. Prisoners inside are also escaping without fear,” he said.Stalin further alleged that the TVK government was incapable of protecting the people of Tamil Nadu, describing it as a “completely useless, good-for-nothing administration”.He said the state had reached a point where people were being left to fend for themselves, and demanded accountability over the security lapses.This is not the first time Stalin has used a cinematic reference to target Vijay's government. Days earlier, he invoked 'Breaking Bad' following a multi-crore methamphetamine seizure in the state.The political attack followed the arrest of Boopalan, a TVK Nagapattinam district functionary and the party's Kilvelur election in-charge, by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI). He was arrested for allegedly harbouring 135kg of methamphetamine, reportedly worth several crores of rupees.According to preliminary investigations, the 17 undertrial inmates allegedly feigned epileptic seizures to lure prison staff into opening their cell before attacking the guards and fleeing the premises.The incident took place at Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district late on Monday night. Four of the escapees have been rearrested, while 13 remain at large.Three prison personnel were injured in the incident. Grade II Police Constable Thangapandi suffered serious head injuries and was rushed to the Government Hospital at G Vilakku. Two other personnel sustained minor injuries.Praveen Kumar was the first of the four escapees to be caught. The other three, identified as Silambarasan of Theni and Raja Sikandar and Rajkumar of Madurai, were re-arrested during search operations on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin launches fresh cinematic salvo at the ruling TVK government. He follows up his 'Breaking Bad' jibe with a 'Prison Break' reference to target chief minister C Joseph Vijay. 17 undertrial inmates allegedly escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Tamil Nadu's Theni district late on Monday night.

Article Title: On Accession Day, Mehbooba blasts Sheikh Abdullah, says his pro-Pak politics turned Kashmiris suspects
Article Text:
Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) President Mehbooba Mufti addresses the gathering during Accession Day, at party office, in Srinagar.

SRINAGAR: PDP president Mehbooba Mufti Monday launched a scathing attack on National Conference founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, accusing him of fuelling anti-India sentiment despite having championed Jammu & Kashmir’s accession to India and providing what she called “Hindutva forces” an opportunity to target the region’s special status.Addressing a party convention at the PDP headquarters here on the occasion of Accession Day (Oct 26), Mehbooba said the people of J&K had willingly joined India and that the country’s initial leadership had maintained good relations with the region and its people.“The first prime minister of the country, Jawaharlal Nehru, had said J&K would be a show window for the world. I do not know what happened between Sheikh Abdullah and the central leadership that Sheikh Abdullah, who was flagbearer of accession, turned against it and began saying we now wanted Pakistan, a plebiscite and separatism,” the former CM said.She said Sheikh Abdullah’s politics strengthened “Hindutva forces” across the country, giving them an excuse to target J&K’s special status and intensify their campaign for “one nation, one flag and one Constitution.”“Sheikh Abdullah was the real flag-bearer of bringing Jammu & Kashmir, a Muslim-majority region, into India. But he became unhappy and launched the plebiscite movement. From 1953, he spent 22 years pursuing that politics.As a result of it, the people of Jammu & Kashmir came to be viewed with suspicion by the country,” she said.“Look at J&K today. It is one of the most militarised regions in the world. There are seven to eight lakh troops including security personnel, paramilitary forces deployed here,” Mehbooba said.She said Sheikh Abdullah returned to the political mainstream in 1975 after reaching an accord with the Centre and abandoned the slogans he had raised for 22 years, including those relating to a plebiscite and Pakistan. However, she said, the people of J&K continued to pay the price for his politics of 22 years.“Even after 80 years, J&K continues to suffer,” she said.Mehbooba said recently at the United Nations, the president of Turkey, who has nothing to do with J&K, raised the issue. As usual, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif also raised it. “In response, our govt said J&K is an integral part of India,” she said.Mehbooba said J&K will be discussed in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh elections, but no one talks about the people of J&K. “Instead, they talk to us through agencies like the NIA and CBI, through the UAPA and the Public Safety Act (PSA),” she said.“India is a great country with a rich culture and heritage, its people are great. But the people of J&K continue to be treated as they were in 1947,” she said. “In 2019, they pushed Jammu & Kashmir into further decline by taking away our rights and abrogating Article 370,” she said.The 79th Accession Day is being celebrated across J&K on Monday. On Oct 26, 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh, the then ruler of the princely state, signed the Instrument of Accession, formally agreeing to Jammu & Kashmir’s accession to India, which came into effect on Oct 27, 1947.
Article Summary: The 79th Accession Day is being celebrated across J&K on Monday. On Oct 26, 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh, the then ruler of the princely state, signed the Instrument of Accession, formally agreeing to Jammu & Kashmir’s accession to India.

Article Title: SC restores Karnataka land, says government can acquire only for public purpose
Article Text:
Supreme Court quashes Karnataka's 1988 acquisition of 59 acres near Bengaluru for a housing society, restores land to owners and orders Rs 50,000 compensation to litigants.

NEW DELHI: Holding that govt can acquire land from citizens only for public purpose and not for the benefit of some person or organisation, Supreme Court Monday quashed a 1988 acquisition of about 59 acres of land near Bengaluru by Karnataka govt for a cooperative housing society and restored the land to its owners after 38 years.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the whole process of land acquisition is indicating “the fraud played on unsuspecting citizens”. It said that illegal acquisitions were made through fraud and undue influence and directed the state govt to pay Rs 50,000 to all litigant landowners who had challenged the process.“Condemnation of privately owned land for public purpose can only be with authority of law and with just compensation being paid. That such authority of law can be exercised only for public purpose is without cavil, with just compensation being an ancillary right, which does not by itself justify an acquisition. However just the compensation be, if the authority of law is lacking or the public purpose is absent, there can be no eminent domain exercised,” the court said.SC upheld the single-bench HC order,which said that it was at the instigation of middlemen that the state employed its machinery to acquire land for the society.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes Karnataka's 1988 acquisition of 59 acres near Bengaluru for a housing society. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the whole process of land acquisition is indicating ‘the fraud played on unsuspecting citizens’

Article Title: The return of student politics: Why campus leaders still matter
Article Text:
When student protests became political movements

DUSU and JNU: Where political careers begin

From Mandal to Assam: When campuses shaped policy

What should student politics actually achieve?

The limits of campus politics

What recent movements tell us about student power

NEW DELHI: From protests over examination irregularities and electoral rolls to debates over caste, education and government policies, students have returned to the streets, raising questions that extend far beyond university campuses. The recent demonstrations in Delhi have once again put student organisations and their leaders in the national spotlight.In October, student activists joined demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protests brought together student groups, political activists and Opposition leaders, turning a dispute over electoral processes into a wider political confrontation.Among those who gained attention was Neha Bora, national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA). Images of Bora being pursued by police in Connaught Place and her subsequent appearance alongside Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during the October 12 march towards the Supreme Court showed how quickly campus activists could move into the national political conversation.But Bora is only one example of a much older phenomenon. Across political ideologies, student organisations have helped mobilise protests, shaped political debates and produced leaders who later entered Parliament and state assemblies.The question is whether today's student movements can have a similar impact, and how effectively they can represent students while navigating national party politics.Student politics in India has a history stretching back to the freedom struggle. Established in 1936, the All India Students' Federation (AISF) was among the earliest nationwide student organisations. After Independence, campuses remained important spaces for political mobilisation.One of the most significant examples came during the Bihar student movement of the 1970s. Protests against corruption, inflation and misgovernance expanded under Jayaprakash Narayan into a mass political movement challenging the Congress government.The movement and the Emergency of 1975 shaped a generation of political leaders. Lalu Prasad Yadav, Nitish Kumar, Sushil Kumar Modi and Ravi Shankar Prasad were among those whose early political careers were influenced by the student activism of that period.Student politics also opened doors for leaders from different political backgrounds. Former Union minister Arun Jaitley and Congress leader Ajay Maken served as Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) presidents. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta began her political journey through the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), meanwhile, produced Left leaders such as Sitaram Yechury and Prakash Karat. Kanhaiya Kumar, who gained national attention during the 2016 JNU controversy, later joined the Congress.These examples show that student politics has not been limited to one party or ideology. For many leaders, campuses provided their first experience of elections, public speaking, organisation and political debate.Delhi University and JNU remain important centres of student politics, although their political cultures differ.At Delhi University, elections are largely contested between the RSS-affiliated ABVP and the Congress-backed National Students' Union of India (NSUI).In the 2026 DUSU elections, ABVP won three of the four central panel posts, with Yash Dabas elected president, Riya Chhawdi secretary and Lakshya Raj Singh joint secretary. Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen, a former NSUI member, won the vice-president's post.The results reflected the continuing influence of national political organisations in campus elections, as well as the ability of independent candidates to challenge them.JNU has traditionally been a stronghold of Left student groups, including AISA and the Students' Federation of India (SFI), although ABVP has also made electoral gains.In 2025, ABVP won the JNUSU joint secretary post and secured 24 of 46 councillor positions in one election. Later that year, the Left Unity alliance swept the central panel, with Aditi Mishra becoming president.Such elections give students experience in political mobilisation, but they also raise questions about whether national party rivalries overshadow concerns about fees, hostels, scholarships and campus infrastructure.Some student movements have influenced debates well beyond university politics.The implementation of the Mandal Commission's recommendation for 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government jobs triggered widespread protests in 1990. The anti-Mandal movement exposed deep divisions over reservation, merit and social justice.In 2016, the death of University of Hyderabad research scholar Rohith Vemula led to nationwide protests over caste discrimination and institutional accountability.Student organisations also played important roles in regional movements.In Assam, the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) led the six-year agitation against alleged illegal immigration that ended with the Assam Accord in 1985. Former AASU leader Prafulla Kumar Mahanta subsequently became chief minister.In Tamil Nadu, student participation in the anti-Hindi agitations of the 1960s helped strengthen the movement against the Congress establishment and brought language politics to the centre of the state's political debate.Students at Osmania University were also active during the movement for a separate Telangana, particularly between 2009 and 2014.More recently, students from Jamia Millia Islamia and Aligarh Muslim University participated in protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act in 2019. At Jadavpur University, the Hokkolorob movement of 2014-15, which followed protests over an alleged molestation case and police action, ended with the resignation of vice-chancellor Abhijit Chakrabarti.The issues and outcomes differed, but these movements demonstrated how student mobilisation could influence public debate, government decisions and political leadership.Despite its connections with national politics, the primary purpose of student unions remains representation within educational institutions.Dr Ashok Sharma, a former JNU student leader, says universities have a responsibility beyond academic learning."Universities are not merely centres of academic learning; they are also spaces where young people develop political awareness, leadership qualities, democratic values and a sense of social responsibility," he says.According to Sharma, elected student representatives must also focus on the everyday concerns of students."Elected representatives have a mandate to raise issues involving academic policies, fees, scholarships, accommodation, campus infrastructure and administrative decisions," he says.However, the close links between student organisations and national political parties can complicate their responsibilities."Many student groups have ideological or organisational affiliations with national political parties, which is not necessarily undesirable because political engagement is part of democratic life. However, problems arise when the priorities of parent political parties overshadow students' academic, administrative and welfare concerns," Sharma says.The challenge, therefore, is not simply to produce future politicians but to ensure that campus politics continues to serve students.Concerns over money, violence and political interference have also shaped how student elections are conducted.The Lyngdoh Committee, appointed in 2005, recommended reforms including eligibility requirements and campaign spending limits. Its recommendations, accepted by the Supreme Court in 2006, set a spending ceiling of Rs 5,000 per candidate.Implementation has differed across universities. Allahabad University, for example, moved from direct student union elections to a student council system in 2019. Supporters argue that such arrangements can reduce disruptions, while critics say they weaken direct student representation.Sharma cautions that student politics should not interfere with education."Excessive politicisation, intimidation, vandalism and prolonged disruptions can undermine academic activities and damage institutional credibility," he says.There is also the question of whether visibility on protest platforms translates into sustained political influence. Many student leaders enter mainstream politics, but not all succeed in building careers beyond their campuses.The growing visibility of student leaders in India's recent protests comes at a time when student activism is also influencing politics elsewhere.In Serbia, protests began after the collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad in November 2024 killed 16 people. Students demanded accountability and organised demonstrations that developed into a broader movement against the government.On October 25, 2026, the student-backed Student List won the country's parliamentary election, with preliminary official results giving it over 52% of the vote. The outcome followed nearly two years of demonstrations and showed how sustained student mobilisation could develop into electoral political power.Serbia's experience is not directly comparable with India's, where student organisations have long-standing links with established political parties. But it shows that movements beginning with specific grievances can develop into wider campaigns.In India, the latest protests have once again brought student leaders into the national conversation. Whether they eventually enter electoral politics or remain activists, their immediate test lies in representing the concerns that brought students together in the first place.Student politics has produced chief ministers, MPs and national leaders. Its larger significance, however, lies in giving young people a platform to question decisions, demand accountability and participate in public life, while ensuring that their educational concerns do not get lost in party politics.
Article Summary: Recent demonstrations in Delhi have once again put student organisations and their leaders in the national spotlight. For many leaders, campuses provided their first experience of elections, public speaking, organisation and political debate. Delhi University and JNU remain important centres of student politics, although their political cultures differ.

NEW DELHI: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam ( DMK ) leader Kanimozhi on Monday criticised Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over the state’s law and order situation, questioning the TVK-led government’s commitment to ensuring women’s safety.In her remarks, Kanimozhi referred to Vijay as “maternal uncle”, referring to the Thaimaman Seer scheme introduced by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government. The scheme's name translates to "maternal uncle's gift" in English.Accusing the Tamil Nadu government of inaction on women’s safety, Kanimozhi cited cases of missing children in Senji and Ranipet, alleging that the administration had failed to take adequate steps to trace them and ensure justice.The DMK deputy general secretary also referred to several incidents, including the murder of a woman in Madurantakam and a violent attack on a family in Thoothukudi. She expressed concern that criminal elements were becoming increasingly emboldened due to alleged political patronage.“They have announced a scheme called ‘Thaimaman Seer’,” Kanimozhi, sister of DMK president and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin , told reporters in Chennai.“But the maternal uncle himself is nowhere to be found. The maternal uncle who is supposed to protect us — where has he gone? That is the situation in Tamil Nadu today,” the Lok Sabha MP remarked.Kanimozhi further alleged that TVK functionaries were directly involved in criminal activities and sexual violence, acting with impunity under the belief that the ruling party would protect them.Referring to Vijay’s earlier remarks on the state’s law and order situation, she questioned, “Is this a (welfare) state or a forest (lawless land)?”The DMK leader also claimed that people across Tamil Nadu felt unsafe and lived in constant fear, both inside and outside their homes.Before assuming office, Vijay had repeatedly criticised the state’s law and order situation and promised to address the issue if elected to power. Kanimozhi pointed out that the same concerns he had previously raised about public safety were now being directed at his own administration.Echoing similar concerns, DMK president MK Stalin had claimed that people were gripped by fear amid what he described as an unprecedented spate of murders, robberies, sexual assaults and cases of missing children in Tamil Nadu over the preceding two months.“Did Vijay predict this in advance and speak like Nostradamus before the election, asking, ‘Is this a country or forest?’ The people who voted believing what they saw on screen — a gun-wielding hero protecting people — have started talking about a hero lacking the substance to prevent crimes,” Stalin wrote in a post on X.
Article Summary: DMK leader Kanimozhi criticised Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over the state’s law and order situation. She accused the Tamil Nadu government of inaction on women's safety. The DMK leader also claimed that people across Tamil Nadu felt unsafe and lived in constant fear.

Accused arrested, licensed pistol seized

Congress raises law and order concerns

GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Police apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting.A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. His condition was stable, a senior doctor said.A forensic and scientific investigation is underway, with specialised teams examining the crime scene and collecting evidence. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. He called on chief minister and home minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to take responsibility and pay greater attention to rising crime.Gogoi, the deputy leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, also called for a thorough inquiry, accountability and concrete measures to prevent similar incidents.
Article Summary: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night. The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker. The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, was arrested within an hour of the incident.

Article Title: 7 civilians killed in Jordan strike on Syrian militants in retaliation to church attack
Article Text:
Syrian authorities reported civilian casualties in Daraa and Sweida after Jordan launched airstrikes against armed groups following Friday’s deadly church attack in Karak (Image credit: Reuters)

Jordan carried out airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria on Tuesday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in the Jordanian city of Karak last week. The strike led to the death of 7 civilians, Syrian authorities said. Moreover, Jordanian authorities said that more than 20 Islamic State militants were killed in airstrikes in southern Syria.Jordan communication minister said that they regreted civilian casualties in Syria and were coordinating with Syrian authorities.Syria’s civil defence agency said seven people were killed in strikes across the southern provinces of Daraa and Sweida. Among them were five members of a family, including three children and a woman, who died when a strike hit a tent in rural Daraa. Three other family members were injured. Two elderly men, aged 80 and 60, were killed in separate strikes, the agency said.Jordan’s air force said the operation killed and wounded several members of the targeted groups and destroyed multiple vehicles. However, it did not identify the groups or disclose the exact locations of the strikes.The Syrian government said the operation was conducted without prior coordination or notification. It said authorities were investigating the incident and had opened communication channels with Jordan to discuss the matter, news agency AP reported.Syria subsequently announced the closure of its main border crossing with Jordan.The strikes came after a gun attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak on Friday killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen others. The attack took place during a funeral in the city, about 90 km south of the Jordanian capital, Amman.Jordanian authorities on Monday arrested three men in connection with the attack following a shootout at dawn. All three were wounded during the operation and taken into custody in Karak.The public security directorate identified the suspects as brothers Hazzah Zaidan Mohammad and Mishal Zaidan Mohammad, and their brother-in-law Ahmad Sami Hussein. All three are Jordanian nationals.The agency’s chief, Major General Obaidallah Abd Rabbo Al-Maayta, described the attackers as “takfiri”, a term commonly used for Sunni militants who label others as apostates. However, he said they were not linked to any organised group and acted on their own. Authorities also recovered a large cache of ammunition from the abandoned house where the men were apprehended.Interior minister Mazen Al-Faraya attributed the attack to extremist ideology, warning that similar incidents could recur if such thinking was not addressed.King Abdullah II had ordered authorities to respond firmly to those responsible, saying that the perpetrators would not escape punishment and that ideologies threatening national unity would not be tolerated.
Article Summary: Jordan carried out airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria on Tuesday. The strikes were in retaliation for a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in the Jordanian city of Karak last week. The strike led to the death of 7 civilians, Syrian authorities said. Jordanian authorities said that more than 20 Islamic State militants were killed in airstrikes.

Article Title: 'Epstein organized many parties with Don': Ex-Miss Switzerland Beatrice Keul accuses Trump of 'brutal' rape
Article Text:
Beatrice Keul and Donald Trump at Plaza Hotel During American Dream World Finals in 1993 (Credit: House Committee on the Judiciary - Democrats report)

What report says

The Epstein link

White House denies allegations

Former Miss Switzerland Beatrice Keul has alleged that US President Donald Trump raped her in 1993 at the Plaza Hotel in New York, describing the alleged assault as “brutal”.Her account features in a new report released by Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee examining Trump's alleged links to Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking operation.Keul, then a young Swiss model and financial services professional, was recruited in November 1993 by Jill Harth to attend the Donald Trump's American Dream Pageant for contestants aged 16 to 22 in Atlantic City and New York.During a press luncheon at the then Trump-owned Plaza Hotel, Trump approached Keul and introduced himself, saying, “Finally we meet Ms Keul”.Later that day, a representative of Trump invited Keul upstairs at the Plaza Hotel to meet the president, according to the report. Believing the meeting could help advance her career and education, she went with the representative.Keul alleged that Trump grabbed her from behind and forcibly raped her upon entering the suite, tearing her dress and leaving her bleeding and bruised. She described the assault as “brutal”.Following the alleged assault, Trump repeated his offers to arrange a visa and university admission and made her promise to remain silent, according to her account.He allegedly told her, “[T]he show must go on.”Keul said she completed the pageant in a terrified “daze”. Her passport had been taken from her on arrival, and she feared that asking for its return before the contest ended would alert Trump that something was wrong, the report said.According to her account, Trump offered to help her obtain a US visa and secure admission to New York University (NYU), repeatedly assuring her that he would take care of her arrangements.After Trump left their conversation, Epstein approached Keul, introducing himself as “I’m Jeffrey, Don’s best friend.” He allegedly offered similar assistance and invited her to a party at Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate in the coming months. “You know I can take care of you. We organize many parties with Don,” Epstein said according to Keul's account.After the assault, she returned to Switzerland and declined to participate in another Trump-sponsored pageant in Hawaii several weeks later. According to the report, Trump called her in Switzerland several months after the alleged assault and again offered to arrange a visa and admission to NYU. She declined.The White House rejected Keul's allegations. “None of these allegations are true,” People quoted White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis as saying.Bis described the report as “nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements.”She added, “The President kicked Jeffrey Epstein out of his club at Mar-a-Lago because he was a creep, and he has been fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein.”Trump has not been charged with a crime in connection with Keul's allegations. The report examines claims concerning his links to Epstein, who was accused of running a sex trafficking operation involving underage girls.(This is a top Google Trends topic.)
Article Summary: Former Miss Switzerland Beatrice Keul has alleged that US President Donald Trump raped her in 1993 at the Plaza Hotel in New York. Her account features in a new report released by Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee examining Trump's alleged links to Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking operation. White House rejected Keul's allegations.

Article Title: Oil prices dip on Iran peace hopes, but Saudi attacks keep Brent near six-month highs
Article Text:
Brent crude fell 0.57% to $115.15 a barrel, while WTI slipped 0.43% to $101.32

Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as fresh diplomatic efforts to ease the US-Israeli war on Iran raised hopes of reduced supply disruptions, although continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept the global benchmark Brent crude near six-month highs.Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.57%, to $115.15 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined 44 cents, or 0.43%, to $101.32 as of 0000 GMT.The decline followed a sharp rally last week, when Brent climbed above $117 a barrel after Iranian attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz heightened concerns over the security of oil shipments. Brent also touched $117 on Monday.Diplomatic efforts offered some relief to markets, with Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan holding talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to ease regional tensions. Riyadh said the visit aimed to establish open channels for negotiations to prevent a renewed military escalation. Iranian state media reported that the four countries agreed to continue discussions on peace and security.However, the prospect of a quick resolution remained uncertain as attacks by Iran-aligned Houthi forces on Saudi Arabia continued to threaten regional stability.October has emerged as the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank tracking maritime security incidents.The conflict has placed the strategic waterway at the centre of global energy concerns. Before the war began in February, the Strait of Hormuz carried around a fifth of the world's energy supplies, making any disruption to shipping a major risk for oil markets.Separately, Russian refiners are increasing diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas following a supply agreement between Moscow and Washington, two industry sources, quoted by Reuters, familiar with the matter said.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.57%, to $115.15 a barrel, while WTI slipped 0.43% to $101.32 a barrel. The decline followed a sharp rally last week, when Brent climbed above $117 a barrel after Iranian attacks on tankers.

Article Title: 'Papa, mai maa ke pass ja rha hu': Jhansi teen records final video, shoots himself with father's pistol
Article Text:
In the Gursarai police station area of Jhansi, a 19-year-old BA student tragically died by suicide.

Video recovered from mobile phone

Father says son was under stress

Police investigation underway





JHANSI: A 19-year-old BA student allegedly died by suicide using his father’s licensed pistol at their home in the Gursarai police station area of Uttar Pradesh’s Jhansi district on Sunday morning.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding his death after recovering a video he recorded on his mobile phone shortly before the incident.The deceased, Love Patel, was the only child of Munna Lal Patel, a retired village development officer who now works in agriculture.Love was found lying inside a room with a gunshot wound after neighbours alerted his family on hearing a gunshot. He was rushed to the Community Health Centre in Gursarai, where doctors declared him dead.Around 8am on Sunday, Munna Lal and his wife, Hemlata, left for the fields, leaving Love alone at home. Around two hours later, neighbours heard a gunshot and rushed to the house but found the door locked from inside.They alerted Munna Lal, who returned and found his son lying on the floor with a gunshot wound. His licensed pistol was found nearby.Police reached the spot and launched an investigation. A forensic team collected evidence, and the body was sent for a post-mortem examination.The video recorded by Love shortly before his death has become a key part of the investigation. In the recording, he reportedly addresses his father emotionally, saying he had caused him considerable distress and continued to trouble him.He then turns the camera towards a photograph of his mother and says, “Papa, paise apne paas rakho, ab mai maa ke paas ja raha hoon” (Dad, keep the money with you. I am going to be with my mother).He reportedly says he does not hold his friends, family members or relatives responsible for his decision.Police are examining the recording and other evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding his death. The reason remains unclear.During questioning, Munna Lal reportedly told police that Love often remained under stress and had difficulty sleeping at night. He said his son sometimes took medication to help him sleep. Police are examining these details, but no cause has been established.Love’s mother, Sangeeta Patel, died by suicide after setting herself on fire in 2009. Love had been living with his father since her death. According to the family, Munna Lal had married Hemlata before marrying Sangeeta, with whom he had Love.Garotha Circle Officer Piyush Kumar Pandey said Love was a resident of Singar village and was pursuing a BA degree.According to the officer, preliminary information indicates that Love locked himself inside a room and shot himself with his father’s licensed pistol. His family took him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Police have questioned Munna Lal, while the forensic team has examined the scene and collected evidence. Investigators are also analysing the mobile phone recording and recording statements from family members to determine the circumstances leading to the incident.
Article Summary: Love Patel, 19, was the only child of Munna Lal Patel, a retired village development officer who now works in agriculture. His mother, Sangeeta Patel, died by suicide after setting herself on fire in 2009. Love was found lying inside a room with a gunshot wound after neighbours alerted his family.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: Father and 33-year-old son killed as old structure caves in at Harsh Vihar
Article Text:
Three bodies were found after a slab of an under-construction house collapsed in Harsh Vihar





NEW DELHI: A 60-year-old man and his 33-year-old son died after a building collapsed in the Harsh Vihar area of Northeast Delhi on Sunday.The deceased have been identified as Chanderpal, 60, and his son, Vijay Kumar, 33. Both were residents of Street number 14 in Harsh Vihar.According to police, information about the collapse at A-4, Milan Garden, was received at the Harsh Vihar police station around 6.46pm on Sunday. A police team subsequently reached the spot.A preliminary inspection revealed that the ground-floor structure of an old building, reportedly being used as a godown, had collapsed along with the first-floor structure above it. The property is reportedly owned by Manoj Kumar.Two fire brigade vehicles, two ambulances and a crane were deployed at the site to assist in the rescue operation. Civil Defence volunteers and a team from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) also joined the efforts.During the overnight rescue operation, the father-son duo was pulled out from beneath the debris and rushed to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital, where doctors declared them brought dead.The rescue operation was still underway, while police initiated legal proceedings under the relevant provisions of law.Further investigation is in progress to ascertain the circumstances that led to the building collapse.
Article Summary: The deceased have been identified as Chanderpal, 60, and his son, Vijay Kumar, 33. Information about the collapse at A-4, Milan Garden, was received at the Harsh Vihar police station. The ground-floor structure of an old building, reportedly being used as a godown, had collapsed.

Article Title: After two decades, Jamia Millia Islamia orders student union polls within 15 days of constitution approval; students reject move, vow to continue stir
Article Text:
Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the holding of students' union elections within 15 days after constitutional approval.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority in resolving the Jamia student protest? Announcing a clear election date Restoring the students’ union Withdrawing disciplinary action Addressing students’ concerns through dialogue 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the resumption of students’ union elections, stating that polls will be held within 15 days of approval of the union’s constitution.The university has also revoked suspension orders and show-cause notices issued to students during the ongoing protest and announced an inquiry into the conduct of security personnel during the agitation.However, protesting students have rejected the administration’s order, calling it ambiguous and insisting that the agitation will continue until their demands are addressed through clear, written commitments.An order issued by Registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi on Monday, October 26, states that elections to the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU) will be held 15 days after the union’s constitution is approved. It also provides for a committee to inquire into the actions of security staff during the protest.The order came after the administration held talks with students who had submitted a list of demands, including the restoration of the elected students’ union, withdrawal of disciplinary action and an inquiry into alleged excesses by security personnel.According to the order, the protesting students have agreed to issue a public apology through a press conference for allegedly defamatory statements, actions or social media posts targeting the university administration during the agitation.The posts are to be taken down from social media platforms with immediate effect.The order states that the protest will be called off immediately following its issuance.However, the Jammu & Kashmir Students Association said the order did not provide a definite timeline for approval of the union’s constitution or address the students’ demand for the resignation of the proctor.“Assurances without concrete decisions and a clear roadmap cannot be treated as fulfilment of our demands,” the student organisation said in a statement, adding that the agitation would continue until the administration provided written commitments addressing their concerns.According to the association, Registrar Rizvi arrived on campus around 4.30am on Monday for talks with the protesters. He shared the administration’s order and urged the students to end their agitation, saying their demands had been met.The protest has centred on the demand for the restoration of JMISU, whose elections have not been held since 2006. Four students had been on an indefinite hunger strike, while other protesters sought a time-bound election schedule, withdrawal of disciplinary action and an inquiry into the conduct of security personnel.Amid escalating tensions, the university had earlier shifted classes across courses to online mode and advised students against visiting the campus. It had also announced that gates and libraries would remain closed until further notice.The administration had said a seven-member committee of professors held multiple rounds of talks with the protesters. A committee to draft the JMISU constitution was notified on October 21.Students, however, had argued that setting up the drafting committee was insufficient without a definite election timeline and student representation in the process.The latest order addresses some of their demands, including the withdrawal of disciplinary action and an inquiry into the conduct of security personnel. However, the lack of a fixed deadline for approval of the constitution remains a key point of contention.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the resumption of students’ union elections. The university has also revoked suspension orders and show-cause notices issued to students during the ongoing protest. However, protesting students have rejected the administration’s order, calling it ambiguous.

Article Title: Kochi Mercedes hit-and-run: Judge’s minor son drives car at high speed, kills man; released on bail, now taken into custody again after protests
Article Text:
A minor driving a Mercedes-Benz collided with a scooter, resulting in the death of a 55-year-old man (L).

A minor behind the wheel of a Mercedes-Benz rammed into a scooter





KOCHI: Police took the 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge into custody again after protests by the family of a man killed when Mercedes-Benz allegedly driven by the minor rammed into his scooter in Cheranelloor, Kochi, in the early hours of Sunday.Police had initially registered a case of causing death by negligence and released the boy on bail from the police station.However, following protests by the victim’s family and a preliminary investigation indicating that the car was being driven at high speed, police invoked Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder.The deceased, Jayabalakrishnan, 55, a resident of South Chittoor, ran a roadside eatery. He was returning home on his scooter after closing his shop when the accident occurred around 2.20am on Container Road near Marapparambu in Cheranelloor.Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery, and a preliminary investigation indicated that the Mercedes hit the scooter from behind. The car is registered in the judge’s name.The initial release of the minor triggered protests outside Cheranelloor police station, where Jayabalakrishnan’s son and daughter, accompanied by activists, demanded that the accused be taken into custody and produced before the Juvenile Justice Board.As the agitation intensified and more people gathered in support of the family, senior police officers intervened. Police subsequently reached the judge’s residence, took the boy into custody and produced him before the board late at night.During the protest, Jayabalakrishnan’s daughter fainted and was taken to hospital, police said.The victim’s family also demanded that a case be registered against the judge for allegedly allowing his minor son to drive the car. Police said they had sought legal opinion on whether the judge could be arraigned in the case and would take a decision on Monday.An earlier police statement said the minor had undergone a medical examination, with preliminary findings indicating that he had not consumed alcohol. A detailed report was awaited.Police sources said the boy had claimed that the scooter suddenly swerved to avoid waterlogging and that he could not stop the car in time to prevent the collision. Heavy rain had lashed the area during the early hours of Sunday.Jayalakshmi, a relative of the victim, described the accident scene as horrifying, pointing to the damage to the vehicles and the distance at which the victim’s footwear and helmet were found.She also alleged that the judge had spoken disrespectfully to the family when they questioned why his minor son had been allowed to drive. The family said it would pursue the case.The incident comes less than three weeks after another fatal crash in Kochi on October 11, when a Mini Cooper allegedly driven at high speed by a 19-year-old who had consumed alcohol hit a scooter, killing three youths. The accused remains in judicial custody.Meanwhile, Youth Congress leader Shajahan P Y had approached state home minister Ramesh Chennithala, seeking action under Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act, which provides for action against the guardian or vehicle owner when a juvenile commits a traffic offence using a vehicle.The law provides for exceptions if the guardian or owner can establish that the offence occurred without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence to prevent it.
Article Summary: Police took the 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge into custody again after protests by the family of a man killed when Mercedes-Benz allegedly driven by the minor rammed into his scooter. Police had initially registered a case of causing death by negligence and released the boy on bail from the police station.

Article Title: 4 killed, several injured as speeding car hits 'Teshu-Jhanjhi' immersion procession in Firozabad
Article Text:
Firozabad DM Santosh Kumar Sharma said the car was seized and the driver and other occupants were taken into custody.

(With agency inputs)





FIROZABAD: Four people, including women and children, were killed and several others injured after a speeding car rammed into a group of villagers on their way to immerse Tesu-Jhenjhi idols in Uttar Pradesh 's Firozabad district.Firozabad district magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma stated that the vehicle involved has been seized, and the driver, along with the other occupants, has been taken into custody."A road accident has occurred involving a car, resulting in four deaths and eight injuries. The victims were walking along the roadside in a group that included many women and children from a village when the accident took place. Arrangements are being made to ensure proper medical treatment for those injured. The vehicle involved has been seized, and the driver, along with the other occupants, has been taken into custody, " Santosh Kumar told news agency ANI."A thorough investigation into the causes of the incident will be conducted. Furthermore, we are reaching out to the Chief Minister's Office to request financial assistance for the families of the deceased. Regarding the cause, while it is a matter for investigation, preliminary reports suggest that the driver may have been under the influence of alcohol; the full picture will emerge once the investigation is complete.Most importantly, this is a deeply tragic incident, " Santosh Kumar added.The district administration is arranging specialised medical treatment for the injured and has approached the Chief Minister’s Office to seek financial assistance for the families of the deceased."The entire administration and the government stand with the bereaved families, and we are committed to providing all possible support, including medical care for the injured and other necessary follow-up actions," district magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma said.Tesu-Jhenjhi is a traditional folk festival celebrated in parts of Uttar Pradesh like Agra, Mathura, Kanpur, Etawah, Orai, and Jhansi.
Article Summary: A speeding car rammed into a group of villagers on their way to immerse Tesu- Jhenjhi idols in Uttar Pradesh's Firozabad district. The victims were walking along the roadside in a group that included many women and children from a village when the accident took place.

Article Title: Pune police write to Google & Apple to take down Rapido from their app stores
